title: Senior's toolkit: modules
summary: Getting, inspecting, upgrading and releasing modules: init and get, modules.json, providers, terraform-docs style READMEs, and the Git commands of a module release.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: modules
steps.body: Module work is half Terraform, half release engineering. These are the commands people who maintain shared modules use.

toolkit.what: Install the modules (and providers) the configuration calls.
flags: newest module versions the `version` constraints allow

toolkit.what: Download or update only the modules, without touching providers or the backend.
Which module call resolved to which source and version, after init.
Which provider each module requires, and with which constraint: who blocks an upgrade?
flags: record checksums for every OS the team uses
the exact schema of the installed providers
one instance of a for_each module

toolkit.cmd: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin main --tags
toolkit.what: Release a module version: tags are what callers pin.
flags: an annotated tag with a message
every caller pinned to it would change silently
toolkit.example: git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Rename nginx to server_block (moved block included)" && git push origin v1.2.0

toolkit.what: Generate the inputs and outputs table for a module README (a separate tool most teams use).
flags: write it into the README between markers
fail CI when the README is out of date

steps.prompt: Match the job to the command.
pairs: see which version of each module init picked
find out which module pins the AWS provider to 5.x

steps.prompt: Semantic versioning for a module: which number goes up?
items: add an optional input with a default
fix a typo in a description
rename a resource without a moved block (callers' plans replace it)
steps.explain: Anything a caller must react to (inputs, outputs, replacements) is major. Additions with safe defaults are minor. Fixes that change no interface and no plan are patches. A rename *with* a `moved` block is safe for callers and can ship in a minor.
